Hi Alyssa — thanks, and great questions. Long answer short: we can support both invoice models but need to confirm how you prefer the reseller margin to be represented on Azure invoices. Below are the options and what we need from you to operationalize each.

Option A — Azure invoice line item (preferred by some resellers):
- Azure issues the invoice, shows the full list price, and includes a pass-through line referencing the reseller margin.
- What we need: reseller legal name, tax ID, and the reseller invoice routing ID used by your ERP. Also a signed reseller statement (we can provide a template).
- Redwood action: we provide the term sheet clause and reseller pass-through mapping for the private offer; engineering tags the offer so invoices include the pass-through code.

Option B — Redwood settles reseller fee downstream (Redwood pays reseller, CloudRetail invoices Redwood/netting):
- Azure invoice shows Redwood as the billed supplier at net price; Redwood issues a settlement to the reseller.
- What we need: reseller payment instructions, settlement cadence (monthly/quarterly), and the reseller contract indicating entitlement.
- Redwood action: set up settlement pipeline (can be batched monthly) and share remittance advices for audit.

Evidence and format: we can accept reseller contracts (PDF), W-9/W-8 forms, or a completed reseller-evidence-template.xlsx (attached). Please also confirm whether the reseller relationship is a direct master agreement or a sub-distributor scenario.

I attached a short term-sheet excerpt showing how we will label pass-through lines and a blank reseller evidence spreadsheet. Ben/Laura — tagging you for the implementation and tax questions.

Next steps: Alyssa, if you can tell us which option you prefer and upload the reseller evidence by EOD Mon we’ll lock the invoice path in the PO schedule and push the final term sheet.

Thanks,
Neha
Head of Marketplace Sales (Redwood Inference)
